source_policy.authority: Supplied source text is authoritative for source-derived claims.
source_policy.preservation_rule: Preserve source terminology, distinctions, examples, standards, taxonomy, use cases, security claims and references without silently correcting or replacing the source.

central_system_flows: Application + configuration + libraries + dependencies -> container -> isolated processes -> shared OS kernel
Container image -> image manifest + filesystem layers + configuration -> container runtime -> container lifecycle
OCI -> Runtime Specification + Image Specification + Distribution Specification -> interoperability
Shared kernel -> security boundary -> possible system-wide security impact

nodes.label: Containerization
nodes.description: Operating-system-level or application-level virtualization over multiple resources allowing applications to run in isolated user spaces called containers across cloud or non-cloud environments.

nodes.label: Container
nodes.description: Isolated user space surrounding an application and bundling related configuration files, libraries and dependencies.

nodes.label: Containerized Computing Environment
nodes.description: Portable computing environment surrounding an application while remaining independent of parallel environments.

nodes.label: Application
nodes.description: Software workload executed within a container.

nodes.label: Isolated User Space
nodes.description: Execution space in which a containerized application and its processes are isolated from other environments.

nodes.label: Isolated Process
nodes.description: Process running inside an isolated container environment.

nodes.label: Container Configuration
nodes.description: Configuration files bundled into a containerized application environment.

nodes.label: Application Library
nodes.description: Library dependency bundled into a container environment.

nodes.label: Application Dependency
nodes.description: Software dependency bundled with an application inside a container.

nodes.label: Operating System Kernel
nodes.description: Common OS kernel shared collectively by multiple containers.

nodes.label: Shared Operating System Kernel
nodes.description: Kernel shared by multiple containers on the same operating-system environment.

nodes.label: Cloud Environment
nodes.description: Cloud computing environment in which containers can run.

nodes.label: Non-cloud Environment
nodes.description: Non-cloud environment in which containers can run.

nodes.label: Vendor Independence
nodes.description: Containerization goal of allowing software to run across environments regardless of cloud/non-cloud type or vendor.

nodes.label: OS Container
nodes.description: Container associated with operating-system-level virtualization.

nodes.label: Application Container
nodes.description: Container associated with application-level containerization.

nodes.label: Container Security Threat
nodes.description: Security threat that can affect a containerized system through its shared operating-system boundary.

nodes.label: Security Scanner
nodes.description: Security scanner that generally protects the operating system but may not protect application containers according to the source.

nodes.label: Container Vulnerability
nodes.description: Application-container vulnerability potentially left unaddressed by OS-focused scanning.

nodes.label: Open Container Initiative
nodes.description: Organization developing open standards for container image formats, runtimes and image distribution.

nodes.label: OCI Runtime Specification
nodes.description: OCI specification defining container configuration, execution environment and lifecycle.

nodes.label: OCI Image Specification
nodes.description: OCI specification defining container image structure including manifests, filesystem layers and configuration.

nodes.label: OCI Distribution Specification
nodes.description: OCI specification governing distribution of container images.

nodes.label: Container Image
nodes.description: Packaged container image whose structure is standardized by OCI.

nodes.label: Image Manifest
nodes.description: Manifest component of a container image defined by the OCI Image Specification.

nodes.label: Filesystem Layer
nodes.description: Filesystem layer forming part of a container image.

nodes.label: Runtime Configuration
nodes.description: Configuration governing a container runtime execution environment.

nodes.label: Container Runtime
nodes.description: Software responsible for the container execution environment and lifecycle.

nodes.label: Container Lifecycle
nodes.description: Creation/execution and lifecycle behavior defined by the container runtime specification.

nodes.label: Container Interoperability
nodes.description: Ability for container images and runtimes to interoperate across implementations and tools.

nodes.label: Container Orchestration
nodes.description: Management/orchestration of containerized applications, particularly application containers.

nodes.label: Container Management
nodes.description: Operational management of containers and containerized applications.

nodes.label: Container Cluster
nodes.description: Cluster of machines/instances running container workloads that requires coordinated management.

nodes.label: Container Cluster Management
nodes.description: Management layer for creating, upgrading, repairing, scaling, balancing and monitoring container clusters.

nodes.label: Cluster Creation
nodes.description: Creation of a container cluster.

nodes.label: Cluster Upgrade
nodes.description: Upgrading software across a container cluster.

nodes.label: Cluster Repair
nodes.description: Repairing cluster software or infrastructure.

nodes.label: Load Balancing
nodes.description: Balancing load across existing container instances.

nodes.label: Container Scaling
nodes.description: Starting or stopping instances to adapt capacity to user demand.

nodes.label: Container Logging
nodes.description: Logging of cluster/application activities.

nodes.label: Container Monitoring
nodes.description: Monitoring cluster, application and sensor output.

nodes.label: Sensor Query
nodes.description: Querying sensors or application state as part of cluster management.

equations.name: Container environment model
equations.expression: Application + configuration + libraries + dependencies -> container -> isolated processes
equations.meaning: Source describes containers as environments surrounding applications and bundling related software dependencies while isolating processes.

equations.name: Shared kernel model
equations.expression: Container_1 + Container_2 + ... + Container_n -> common OS kernel
equations.meaning: Multiple containers collectively share a common operating-system kernel.

equations.name: Container portability model
equations.expression: Bundled application environment + compatible runtime -> cloud/non-cloud deployment across vendors
equations.meaning: Containerization is framed as allowing applications to run across cloud or non-cloud environments regardless of vendor.

equations.name: OCI interoperability model
equations.expression: Standard image + standard runtime + standard distribution -> interoperability across implementations/tools
equations.meaning: OCI specifications are intended to make images and runtimes interoperable across implementations and tools.

equations.name: Container runtime lifecycle
equations.expression: Runtime configuration -> execution environment -> container lifecycle
equations.meaning: OCI Runtime Specification defines configuration, execution environment and lifecycle.

equations.name: Container image structure
equations.meaning: OCI Image Specification defines these image components.

equations.name: Container cluster management
equations.expression: Cluster management = create + upgrade + repair + balance + scale + log + monitor
equations.meaning: Source lists these as cluster management functions.

equations.name: Demand-responsive scaling
equations.expression: User demand change -> start/stop instances -> adjusted capacity
equations.meaning: Cluster management adapts capacity to number of users by starting or stopping instances.

equations.name: Shared-kernel security boundary
equations.expression: Shared OS kernel -> common attack surface -> possible system-wide impact
equations.meaning: Source warns that shared OS architecture can allow security threats to affect the whole containerized system.

equations.name: Container orchestration
equations.expression: Application containers + orchestration controller -> coordinated container management
equations.meaning: Orchestration is mainly used for application containers and includes Kubernetes and Docker Swarm.

source_claims.claim: Containerization is OS-level or application-level virtualization enabling isolated user spaces across cloud or non-cloud environments.
Containers surround applications, bundle configuration/libraries/dependencies, isolate processes, and collectively share an OS kernel.
Containerization is widely adopted by major cloud platforms and pursued by the U.S. Department of Defense, first applied to the F-22.
Shared OS architecture creates security concerns and OS-focused scanning may leave application containers insufficiently protected.
OCI develops Runtime, Image and Distribution specifications intended to provide interoperability.
Container orchestration/management is mainly used for application containers, with Kubernetes and Docker Swarm named as implementations.
Container cluster management includes creation, upgrade, repair, load balancing, scaling, logging and monitoring.
The source provides journal literature covering containerization technologies, applications, challenges and cloud distributed systems.
The source provides books on containerization and Docker.
The source provides additional references including Kubernetes, Red Hat, IBM, OCI and orchestration resources.

historical_events.event: Containerization became widely adopted by major cloud platforms.
The U.S. Department of Defense pursued containerization for faster software development and fielding, with first application in the F-22.
OCI maintains Runtime, Image and Distribution specifications for container interoperability.

semantic_distinctions.name: Container vs Virtual Machine
semantic_distinctions.description: Containerization uses OS/application-level virtualization and shared kernels; system VMs can provide whole-machine/guest-OS abstractions.

semantic_distinctions.name: OS Container vs Application Container
semantic_distinctions.description: Source identifies OS containers and application containers as distinct container types.

semantic_distinctions.name: Container vs Container Image
semantic_distinctions.description: Container is an execution environment; image is a packaged artifact whose structure is standardized by OCI.

semantic_distinctions.name: Image vs Runtime
semantic_distinctions.description: Image describes packaged filesystem/configuration content; runtime defines execution environment and lifecycle.

semantic_distinctions.name: Runtime Specification vs Image Specification
semantic_distinctions.description: Runtime Specification covers execution/lifecycle; Image Specification covers image structure.

semantic_distinctions.name: OCI Distribution vs Image Specification
semantic_distinctions.description: Distribution concerns image distribution; Image Specification concerns image representation.

semantic_distinctions.name: Container Management vs Orchestration
semantic_distinctions.description: Management encompasses operational functions; orchestration specifically coordinates application containers.

semantic_distinctions.name: Orchestration vs Cluster Management
semantic_distinctions.description: Orchestration coordinates application containers; cluster management covers infrastructure/cluster lifecycle, scaling and observability.

semantic_distinctions.name: Shared Kernel vs Separate Guest OS
semantic_distinctions.description: Containers share a kernel; system VMs provide guest OS execution.

semantic_distinctions.name: Portability vs Interoperability
semantic_distinctions.description: Portability concerns running across environments/vendors; interoperability concerns compatible implementations/tools under common standards.

semantic_distinctions.name: OS Security Scanning vs Application Security
semantic_distinctions.description: Protecting the host OS does not necessarily protect application containers.

semantic_distinctions.name: Scaling vs Load Balancing
semantic_distinctions.description: Scaling changes the number of instances; load balancing distributes load among existing instances.

semantic_distinctions.name: Logging vs Monitoring
semantic_distinctions.description: Logging records activities; monitoring observes logs, applications or sensors.

semantic_distinctions.name: Container Runtime vs Container Manager
semantic_distinctions.description: Runtime implements execution/lifecycle; manager/orchestrator manages groups/workloads.

semantic_distinctions.name: Cloud vs Non-cloud Container Deployment
semantic_distinctions.description: Containerization explicitly spans both cloud and non-cloud environments.

semantic_distinctions.name: Container Security Benefit vs Security Risk
semantic_distinctions.description: Isolation provides separation, but shared-kernel architecture creates a broader security concern.

semantic_distinctions.name: Cluster Repair vs Upgrade
semantic_distinctions.description: Repair restores operational state; upgrade changes software versions/state.

semantic_distinctions.name: Application Dependency vs Kernel Dependency
semantic_distinctions.description: Libraries/configuration/dependencies are bundled per application; containers still depend on a shared OS kernel.

misconceptions.misconception: Containers are just small virtual machines.
misconceptions.correction: The source frames containers as OS/application-level virtualization and emphasizes shared kernel operation.

misconceptions.misconception: Every container has its own operating-system kernel.
misconceptions.correction: Multiple containers collectively share a common OS kernel.

misconceptions.misconception: A container is the same thing as a container image.
misconceptions.correction: The image is the packaged artifact; the container is the execution environment.
OCI maintains Runtime, Image and Distribution specifications.

misconceptions.misconception: OCI Runtime Specification defines image layers.
misconceptions.correction: Runtime Specification defines configuration/execution/lifecycle; image layers belong to Image Specification.

misconceptions.misconception: Orchestration and cluster management are identical.
misconceptions.correction: The source distinguishes application-container orchestration from broader cluster management functions.
Scaling changes instance count; load balancing balances work among existing instances.

misconceptions.misconception: OS security scanning automatically secures application containers.
misconceptions.correction: The source explicitly warns that scanners generally protect the OS but may not protect application containers.

misconceptions.misconception: Containerization only applies to public cloud.
misconceptions.correction: The source explicitly includes non-cloud environments.

misconceptions.misconception: Containerization eliminates security risk through isolation.
misconceptions.correction: The shared OS can allow security threats to affect the whole containerized system.

misconceptions.misconception: Kubernetes is the only container orchestrator.
misconceptions.correction: The source names both Kubernetes and Docker Swarm and its taxonomy also lists OpenShift and Amazon ECS.
The source lists creation, upgrades, repair, balancing, scaling, logging and monitoring.

why_it_matters.core_problem: Package applications into isolated, portable environments while sharing operating-system resources and coordinating those environments at cluster scale.
why_it_matters.mechanism_chain: Application dependencies/configuration -> container artifact/runtime -> isolated process environment -> shared kernel -> orchestration -> cluster management -> scaling/observability.
why_it_matters.central_insight: Containerization is not merely packaging software. In the supplied source it is a layered system spanning virtualization boundaries, application packaging, standardized images/runtimes/distribution, orchestration and cluster operations, with a distinct shared-kernel security model.
